hydralazine.watch: Low BP, fast heart rate, headache
hydralazine.nursing: Check BP before and 15–30 min after. Look-alike: hydrOXYzine.

hydroxyzine.watch: Sedation, confusion in older adults, QT prolongation

trazodone.watch: Drowsiness, low BP when standing, QT prolongation

quetiapine.nursing: Preferred over haloperidol in Parkinson’s disease.

melatonin.nursing: Safer first choice for sleep in older adults.

lisinopril.watch: Low BP, high potassium, dry cough, face or tongue swelling (angioedema)
lisinopril.nursing: Check BP and potassium before giving. Not for use in pregnancy.

metoprolol.use: Blood pressure, heart failure, heart rate control
metoprolol.watch: Slow heart rate, low BP, fatigue
metoprolol.nursing: Check heart rate and BP before giving. Do not stop suddenly.

furosemide.nursing: Daily weight, intake and output, potassium.

metformin.nursing: Hold before IV contrast and when kidney function is below 30.

insulin.nursing: Check glucose, give within 15 min of a meal, independent double-check.

enoxaparin.nursing: Check platelets and kidney function. Do not expel the air bubble.

warfarin.nursing: Check INR. Many drug and food (vitamin K) interactions.

diltiazem.nursing: Check heart rate and BP. Do not crush ER tablets.

atorvastatin.nursing: Watch for interactions with azole antifungals and some antibiotics.

acetaminophen.watch: Liver injury above 4 g a day
acetaminophen.nursing: Count every source, including combination pills.

morphine.nursing: Check sedation level, RR and SpO2 before and after. Naloxone at the bedside.

ondansetron.nursing: Safe antiemetic choice in Parkinson’s disease.

ceftriaxone.nursing: Give on schedule to keep levels steady.

diphenhydramine.watch: Sedation, confusion, falls in older adults
diphenhydramine.nursing: On the Beers list for patients 65+.

prednisone.watch: High blood sugar, mood changes, infection risk
prednisone.nursing: Give with food. Check glucose in diabetes.

albuterol.watch: Fast heart rate, tremor, low potassium
albuterol.nursing: Check lung sounds and heart rate after.

doxycycline.nursing: Take upright with a full glass of water. Avoid in pregnancy.

metronidazole.nursing: No alcohol during and 3 days after.

labetalol.watch: Low BP, slow heart rate, dizziness
labetalol.nursing: Check BP and heart rate before giving.

nifedipine.nursing: Do not crush the ER tablet.

carbidopa.watch: Nausea, low BP when standing, involuntary movements
carbidopa.nursing: Give within 30 min of the scheduled time. Late doses cause stiffness and swallowing problems.

pantoprazole.nursing: IV push over at least 2 minutes.

piperacillin.nursing: Draw blood cultures first. First dose within 1 hour in sepsis.

vancomycin.watch: Kidney injury, flushing if infused too fast
vancomycin.nursing: Infuse slowly (at least 60 min per gram). Dosing guided by blood levels.

hydrocodone.watch: Sedation, slowed breathing, liver injury from acetaminophen

ibuprofen.watch: Stomach bleeding, kidney injury, higher BP
ibuprofen.nursing: Avoid with warfarin, kidney disease, heart failure, GI bleed and late pregnancy.

tramadol.nursing: Avoid with other opioids and benzodiazepines.

codeine.watch: Nausea, sedation; effect varies by person

lorazepam.nursing: Never combine with opioids without close monitoring.

zolpidem.nursing: Avoid in older adults when possible.

verapamil.nursing: Avoid with beta-blockers and in heart failure.

potassium.nursing: Check potassium first. Never give IV push.

glipizide.nursing: Higher risk with kidney disease and with insulin.

pioglitazone.nursing: Boxed warning: avoid in heart failure.
